G01.notes: All three explain financial incentives and disclosures, but none states the safety-washing or actuarial-hype point.

G02.notes: The four study-specific regime descriptions are supported. A's shared controls proposal is labeled and grounded in observed regulatory differences.

G03.misleading_claims: G03-C F1: The cited passages do not substantiate transfer across model sizes without regenerating adversarial examples.
G03.notes: A states SCR mechanics in a cited limitation. B and C get the cost half of G03.5. C reports a different attack setting, so its pairs do not satisfy the known-attack requirement. Quotes alone do not earn credit.

G04.notes: A describes part of Pandora's mechanism, but its published findings and limitations never state the numerical results quoted under L0. B omits the numeric naive baseline. C's 96% is for one model and does not satisfy the ten-model average. B and C describe moderation stealth but omit the token-wise defense result.

G05.notes: A states parity without the participant counts. B's cited limitations establish the Chinese records used in MVME. C omits that population context and does not explicitly say dispute resolution improved performance. The supervised pilot interpretations are conditional and make no readiness claim.

G06.notes: 53% is source-reported rounding, but all omit the median. A and C omit the group cutoffs and dispersion in G06.2. C correctly attributes 17% and 22.9% to different sections and gives the zero count, so credit G06.3 without flagging either attributed figure.

G07.notes: All omit GPT-4o-mini's exact score and the exact untuned base score. B gives 7B accuracy but omits speed, and does not state the SME exclusion. A earns the scope point by faithfully attributing the narrower scope to the limitations section and noting the conflicting database description.

G08.notes: 86.4% is the source precision for the rounded 86% requirement. A and B give both accuracy values and the study's qualitative small overhead. C cites a compute measure but does not state the small overhead. B identifies one of four model names.

G09.notes: A's cited STARD Recall@10 and MRR@10 are valid but distinct from the requested MAS+GRPO Recall@14/HitRate@14 results. C omits the zero-shot commercial Qwen-Max identification. All distinguish compute proxies from monetary prices and state Chinese-only scope.

G10.notes: B and C explicitly say the deployment rate is unavailable and identify the controlled-game reason, which satisfies both components. They do not state the requested game setup or outcome figures. A has no published content.
